<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/service-automation`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **10** documentable anchor(s).

**5** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/api/client-sdk.mdx`  _(via AutomationResult (symbol, a top-level interface))_
- `content/docs/api/declarative-endpoints.mdx`  _(via /api/v1/automation/:name/trigger (route, bridged from symbol TriggerFlowResponseSchema — its route source's handler names it))_
- `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx`  _(via AutomationResult (symbol, a top-level interface), bubbleToParent (symbol, a method of class AutomationEngine), /api/v1/automation/:name/trigger (route, bridged from symbol TriggerFlowResponseSchema — its route source's handler names it))_
- `content/docs/kernel/cluster.mdx`  _(via AutomationEngine (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/http-protocol.mdx`  _(via /api/v1/automation/:name/trigger (route, bridged from symbol TriggerFlowResponseSchema — its route source's handler names it))_

⛔ **5** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v16.mdx`  _(via AutomationEngine (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via AutomationEngine (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-1.mdx`  _(via AutomationResult (symbol, a top-level interface))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-3.mdx`  _(via AutomationResult (symbol, a top-level interface))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via AutomationEngine (symbol, a top-level class), AutomationResult (symbol, a top-level interface))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **171** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0a5035757602ec5ad6b580e9f535496cd3bd8579` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `2786df4085e1be8cfd8816bfe966676d17119276` — the merge of head `d7a8d98fcf7685b467abcb64605fc52d57e724d7` into base `0a5035757602ec5ad6b580e9f535496cd3bd8579`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 2786df4085e1be8cfd8816bfe966676d17119276 && git checkout 2786df4085e1be8cfd8816bfe966676d17119276
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 0a5035757602ec5ad6b580e9f535496cd3bd8579 d7a8d98fcf7685b467abcb64605fc52d57e724d7 && git checkout -B drift-repro 0a5035757602ec5ad6b580e9f535496cd3bd8579 && git merge --no-ff d7a8d98fcf7685b467abcb64605fc52d57e724d7

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0a5035757602ec5ad6b580e9f535496cd3bd8579
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 0a5035757602ec5ad6b580e9f535496cd3bd8579` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `fb720b6cbb82e4c7e74438044da889ccf09e5c60`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/automation-api.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/contracts/automation-service.ts + packages/services/service-automation/src/engine.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/run-dropped-fields.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/run-resume.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/builtin/map-node.ts

Widened, read and graded because the brief asked: `packages/services/service-automation/src/run-dropped-fields.test.ts`, `.changeset/33019-flow-answer-delegated-dropped-fields.md`, and the regenerated `content/docs/references/api/automation-api.mdx`. Read at this head, never reviewed: `builtin/subflow-node.ts`, `dag-traversal.ts` (step writing, region suspension), `run-resume.ts` outside the hunks (the map-item gate, the cancelled-item continuation, the refusal arm), spec `data/data-engine.zod.ts`, `.changeset/32861-flow-answer-dropped-fields.md`, AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist item 3. Prior records 6843734657 and 6844555869 on PR #33007 were read; this PR is the follow-up their S1 and N1 named.

Check-runs on this head, read 2026-11-13 (twice, same counts): 24 success, 10 skipped, 31 in_progress, 0 failed.
- Green: every lint job, `Type Check · source gates`, `Check Changeset`, `PR-body guards`, `Spec property liveness`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Check Documentation Links`, `Check PR Size`.
- Not concluded: Test Core 1 to 8, Test UI 1 to 16, `Build Core`, `Build Docs`, `Build & E2E UI`, `Live E2E UI`, and the workspace, UI, consumer-gates and debt-ledger type checks.
- The shard that runs the 8 new cases, the workspace type check and the docs build are among those still running. Their green rests on the dev report until the seat re-reads before queueing.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **No accept set and no type moves: right.** The `automation-api.zod.ts` hunk is one `//` comment and the describe string; `z.array(DroppedFieldsEventSchema).optional()` is untouched. The `automation-service.ts` hunk is jsdoc only; `droppedFields?: DroppedFieldsEvent[]` is untouched. The parity guard between the two members has nothing new to bind.
2. **The behaviour is a widening of what the answer carries: right.** The member now appears on a terminal success in two shapes where it was absent before (a `map` item that dropped; a `subflow` or `map` child that paused and resumed). Shape, omit-when-empty and "terminal success only" are unchanged.
3. **The widening is exactly the card's Expected: right.** Every leg that credits a child's totals to the parent's `summary` now also folds the child's drops. Read leg by leg in ④; no leg that `summary` credits on a completed child is left out, and no leg is added that `summary` does not credit.
4. **`Clause-②: yes (widening)` rather than the card's tentative `none`: right.** The card said to judge at the time. A published answer member is set in situations where it was not, and the published describe changes its promise, so the conservative arm is the true one. The claim (6845576912) declared the same line before the first push.
5. **`Metadata-protocol: none`: right.** Nothing a metadata author can write changes.
6. **Skipping malformed events is not an undeclared narrowing: right.** The answer's element was always `DroppedFieldsEventSchema`; an event outside it (an unknown `reason`, `fields` not a list) was never inside the contract, and both in-tree producers are well-typed. The changeset's second bullet states the skip.
7. **No new vocabulary: right.** One fold, the engine's own event, one event per object and reason.

### ② Semver level

- **`patch` on `@objectstack/spec` and `@objectstack/service-automation`: right.** AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist item 3: the level follows the kind alone, `none` takes `patch`, and a non-protocol widening ships `patch`. `Check Changeset` is green on this head.
- **Declaration lines: identical.** `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` are line-initial and the same in the PR body and the changeset.
- **Changeset prose against the tree: true but for one phrase.** The three bullets match the code (map synchronous and pausing exits, both resumed legs, the total fold, the member's shape unchanged). "What remains: a child run that failed answers no drops" reads as the whole remainder and is not; see S2.
- **nit (changeset prose): two unreleased entries will ship side by side and disagree.** `.changeset/32861-flow-answer-dropped-fields.md` still says a paused child and a `map` item "do not yet" roll up. The new entry says it lifts that. CHANGELOG order within one release is not by card number. Editing the unreleased #32861 sentence is cleaner; the PR declares the choice, so it is accepted as written.
- **Docs page: agrees.** The `droppedFields` row in `content/docs/references/api/automation-api.mdx` equals the new describe string character for character and carries no card id. Its type column is unchanged, as the schema is.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **File surface: held.** The nine files are inside the claim's surface. `builtin/subflow-node.ts` was claimed and is untouched; its synchronous roll-up already reads the child's answer, which is the fold's output.
- **Card id kept out of the describe: right.** #33019 sits in the adjacent `//` comment and in the jsdoc, as `check:doc-authoring` requires; the lint job that runs it is green.
- **Out-of-scope finding "carrier: none" (a failed child answers no drops): accepted as stated, and published.** Carrying drops on a failed answer would widen the failure shape of `AutomationResult`; that is a spec decision and is rightly not taken here.
- **Run history: a wire member grows, undeclared, under an open carrier.** `steps[].droppedFields` is persisted and served by the runs routes; `ExecutionStepLogSchema` does not declare it (#33020, open). After this PR a `map` step, and a `subflow` or `map` step credited on resume, also carry it, and a `map` step with status `failure` can carry it. #33020 should be told its scope grew. See N2.
- **`Fixes #33019` with #32861 named in prose: right.** #32861 stays open for its console half #33009.
- **`main` moved past the merge base `c54a23d2` to `157051ce`.** The merged tree is the queue's to run.
- **PR author is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`:** no off-relay login to name.

### ④ Design judgment

**must-fix: none.**

**What holds, read in the tree**

- **`automation-api.zod.ts` (hit).** Each new sentence is true of the code.
  - "a `subflow` child's run and each `map` item's run, whether it completed without pausing or paused and resumed": true on all five legs, listed under the implementing files below.
  - "A child run that failed answers no drops": true. Only the three terminal-success exits set the member; `subflow-node.ts` and `map-node.ts` read nothing from a failed child.
  - "where a `try_catch` or `fault` edge contains that failure an absent member is not proof": true, and the earlier items' drops still answer (the map's failure exit).
  - First consumer (#33009, the console reader): the entry shape it parses is unchanged; it only receives events in more cases.
- **`automation-service.ts` (hit).** The jsdoc says the same as the describe, adds "as {@link summary} credits them" (true: the same seams) and "Unlike `summary`, a child run that FAILED answers no drops" (true: the failure arms roll the failed child's totals and no drops).
- **`run-dropped-fields.ts`.** `dropEventsOf` is now `foldDropEvents` over the steps' lists, so there is one fold. It skips a list that is not an array and an event that fails `DroppedFieldsEventSchema.safeParse`, copies `fields`, and answers `undefined` for nothing. This closes N1 of record 6843734657: the three callers inside a `try` (the terminal exits) can no longer throw over a host executor's value.
- **`builtin/map-node.ts`.** `itemDrops` is per entry, like the totals, and is pushed only on synchronous completion. All four exits spread `rolledDrops()`. `dag-traversal.ts` copies an executor's `droppedFields` onto the step on the success, suspend, refuse and failure arms, so each exit's value reaches the step log.
- **`run-resume.ts` and `engine.ts`.** `creditChildRun` folds the child's events with whatever the awaiting step already holds, onto the same step its totals land on. Both callers pass them: the up-bubble (`childDroppedFields`, handed in by `bubbleToParent`) and the delegated leg (`childRes.droppedFields`). The terminal exit computes `dropEventsOf(steps)` once for its answer and its up-bubble. `RunResumeHost` types these three members off `AutomationEngine`, so the new trailing parameters need no second declaration.
- **Every path, by reading.**
  - Direct `map`, items complete synchronously: the completion exit. Reported.
  - `map`, an earlier item completed and a later one pauses: the suspend exit holds the earlier drops; the paused item's are credited on its bubble; the re-entry writes a fresh step. Reported.
  - `map`, item resumed: only the up-bubble exists (resuming the parent while an item is parked is refused `MAP_ITEM_PENDING`). Reported.
  - `subflow`, synchronous: unchanged from #33007. Reported.
  - `subflow`, paused then resumed through the parent's id (delegated) or its own (up-bubble): reported. Chains of any depth follow by induction, because each frame's answer is the fold of its credited steps.
  - A drop before the child's own pause: in the child's whole-run answer, so it rides the same seam.
  - Refused child: the parent refuses and a refused answer carries none; the refusal arm of `bubbleToParent` passes none. Consistent.
  - A pause inside a structured region is refused by the engine, so there is no region leg to credit.
  - Failed child: not reported, declared.
  - Cancelled paused `map` item: not reported, not declared. See S2.
- **Existing callers.** A run with no `map` and no paused child answers byte for byte as before, unless a host executor returned an event outside the schema, which is now skipped (declared). The `execute()` and retried-attempt exits are untouched and read the same fold.

**should-fix S1 (pins, `run-dropped-fields.test.ts`): two added behaviours stay green when cut.**
- **The map's failure exit.** No case runs an item that drops, then an item that fails, under a `try_catch` or `fault` edge. Deleting `...rolledDrops()` at that exit leaves all 16 green. The PR's ablation list (A to G) has no cut for it, yet the code comment and the describe both rest on it.
- **The merge in `creditChildRun`.** No case credits a child's drops onto a step that already holds some. In the earlier-item case the paused item drops nothing, so the credit is skipped; in the up-bubble and delegated cases the awaiting step holds none. Replacing `foldDropEvents([steps[i].droppedFields, childDroppedFields])` with the child's list alone leaves all 16 green, and would erase the earlier items' drops.
- One case closes both: `map` over two items where the first drops field A synchronously and the second pauses, resumes and drops field B; expect both. A second, small case closes the failure exit.
- The other legs are pinned and the reported reds are what the code predicts: A (map synchronous), B and D (both up-bubble cases), C (delegated), E (suspend exit), F (the `safeParse` guard). G reds 11 because the guard also skips the `undefined` list of a drop-free step, so it does not isolate the not-a-list case; the PR says so.

**should-fix S2 (both hits and the changeset): the failed child is not the only leg that still answers no drops.**
- A `map` item that wrote and dropped, then paused, and whose run an operator cancelled (#27971): `continuePastCancelledMapItem` lets the map go on with a marker in the item's slot, the parent completes, and nothing of the item's run reaches the parent. `summary` does not credit it either, so the card's rule holds; the published remainder does not.
- The describe and jsdoc narrowed "absent is not proof" from every delegated write to the failed child alone, and the changeset says "What remains". The #33009 reader will take absence as proof everywhere else.
- Smallest fix: one clause on both hits and the regenerated mdx naming the cancelled item beside the failed child, or a carrier card that does it. The marker in `results` already tells a caller the item did not finish.

**nit N1: the refusal exit's `...rolledDrops()` cannot reach an answer.** A refused run's answer carries no `droppedFields`. The spread only writes the completed items' events to the step log. Harmless symmetry with the totals.

**nit N2: the step log keeps what the answer skips.** `dag-traversal.ts` puts any `droppedFields` with a truthy `length` on the step, so a host executor's malformed value is persisted and served by the runs routes verbatim while the fold drops it from the answer. Carry on #33020 with the wider step coverage noted in ③.

**nit N3: `creditChildRun`'s "drops but no summary" branch is unreachable.** Both callers pass a summary whenever they pass drops. The early `return` it adds is dead today.

**nit N4: no case runs a chain deeper than two, and none runs on the durable store.** Both hold by reading (induction over the terminal exit; the step log is persisted whole). N6 of record 6843734657 stands as accepted.
